t: Palindromic Path Queries in a Tree
o: A path's characters can be rearranged into a palindrome iff at most one character occurs an odd number of times on the path. We must answer such queries online, interleaved with single-node character updates, on trees with n, q up to 5e4. Root the tree; the path u-v consists of the root-to-u and root-to-v paths spliced at their LCA.
k: Encode each node's letter as a 26-bit mask; the path mask is X(u) XOR X(v) XOR bit(letter at LCA), where X(v) is the root-to-v XOR — the LCA's bit is counted twice in X(u)^X(v) and must be restored once.
Character updates change X for a whole subtree; store X in a Fenwick tree over the Euler tour so an update is a range XOR and a query is a prefix XOR.
Answer each query by checking popcount(pathMask) <= 1 after finding the LCA with binary lifting.

a.n: Euler-tour Fenwick XOR + binary lifting LCA
a.i: Compute tin/tout, depths, and ancestor table once. Maintain X(v) = XOR of letter masks on root-to-v path inside a Fenwick tree indexed by tin: setting a node's letter XOR-updates the range [tin, tout] of its subtree (point query = prefix XOR at tin). Each query is then O(log n) for the LCA plus O(log n) for two prefix-XOR reads and a popcount.
s: Root at 0; iterative DFS for tin, tout, depth, immediate parents; build binary lifting table.
Fenwick over Euler positions supporting XOR range-update, prefix-XOR point-query; initialize with each node's letter over its subtree range.
Update (u, c): XOR-delta = oldBit ^ newBit applied to u's subtree range.
Query (u, v): w = LCA(u,v); mask = X(u)^X(v)^bit(w); answer popcount(mask) <= 1.
a.t: O((n + q) log n) — DFS/lifting-table build is O(n log n); each update or query touches O(log n) Fenwick nodes plus an O(log n) LCA
a.sp: O(n log n) — binary lifting table dominates

w: This is the standard online path-query toolkit: Euler tour + Fenwick for subtree updates, binary lifting for LCA, bitmask parity for rearrangeability. Pitfalls: forgetting to re-add the LCA's own bit (it cancels in X(u)^X(v)), using recursion (stack overflow at 5e4 depth), and 32-bit issues (26-bit masks fit comfortably in int). Follow-up: report the minimum number of changes to make the path a palindrome (answer = max(0, oddCount/2 adjustments)), or handle edge-weighted paths.
